steps.title: Frame FIR-01 as one symmetric channel filter per DDC channel, DSP-count-first
steps.goal: Write the Overview: what one FIR-01 instance does, how the 32 instances relate to the DDC, and the design priorities (DSP count over latency, sustained 1 sample/clk at 491.52 MHz).

spec_evidence.quote: each channel needs a linear-phase
one new sample every clock, 491.52 MHz on a Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoC
so DSP slice count matters more than latency.
Throughput: one input and one output sample per clock, sustained.

options: One fully parallel FIR instance per channel (32 instances)
Time-multiplexed FIR shared across channels
decisions.choice: One fully parallel FIR instance per channel; 32 instances in the system
decisions.rationale: Each channel delivers one new sample every fabric clock, so there is no spare cycle to time-share multipliers between channels.

done_when: Overview states one instance = one channel, 1 in/1 out sample per clock at 491.52 MHz
Priority order (DSP count > fabric > latency) is stated explicitly
Per-instance and 32-channel DSP48E2 counts for N_TAPS=16 and N_TAPS=64 are quoted (ceil(N_TAPS/2) per instance)
Overview states that each instance owns its coefficient bank and that the wrapper may broadcast writes to all 32 channels

steps.title: Define the N_TAPS generic, sample/valid ports and per-instance coefficient write port
steps.goal: Specify the Parameters (N_TAPS default 16, legal 2-64, widths) and the Interface (sample in/valid, sample out/valid, per-instance coefficient write port and commit driven by the existing AXI-Lite wrapper, which may broadcast).

spec_evidence.quote: Linear-phase FIR with a configurable number of taps N (16 for the first product; up to 64 later).
Both even and odd N must be supported.
Input: 16-bit signed samples, Q1.15. Output: 16-bit signed, Q1.15.
Coefficients: 18-bit signed, Q1.17.
They must be loadable at run time from the control processor (via a simple write port; the AXI-Lite wrapper exists already).
The upstream decimator provides a valid signal.

options: Synthesis-time generic N (structure sized per build)
Runtime-programmable tap count up to 64
decisions.choice: N_TAPS is a synthesis parameter (default 16, legal range 2-64, even or odd); only coefficient values change at run time, via the shadow bank and commit
decisions.rationale: User answer Q1. Sizing the DSP chain to N_TAPS is what saves DSPs for the N=16 product.

options: Independent coefficient bank per instance (wrapper may broadcast writes)
Single coefficient bank shared by all 32 channels
decisions.choice: Each instance holds its own coefficient bank and write port; the wrapper can broadcast one write to all channels
decisions.rationale: User answer Q2 accepted this default; keeps the core self-contained and supports per-channel filters.

done_when: Parameter table lists N_TAPS (default 16, legal 2-64), input/coef/output widths and formats, and derived values (number of DSPs = ceil(N_TAPS/2), coefficient address width)
Elaboration-time check rejects N_TAPS outside 2..64
Port table gives name, direction, width, format and clock domain for every port, including coefficient address/data/write-enable/commit
Odd vs even N_TAPS effect on the address map is stated (ceil(N_TAPS/2) unique coefficients written)
Broadcast usage by the wrapper (same write/commit to all instances) is described as a wrapper feature requiring no core change

steps.title: Make the transposed-vs-systolic call with symmetric pre-adder mapping on DSP48E2
steps.goal: Choose the filter structure, justify it against transposed form, and draw the Block Diagram showing the DSP chain, pre-adder operand sourcing, cascades and centre-tap handling for odd N_TAPS.

spec_evidence.quote: The team has argued about using the transposed form or a systolic
Please make the call in the micro-architecture and document why.
Exploit symmetry to halve the multiplier count.
The design should map onto DSP48E2 slices using dedicated cascade routing where possible.
The impulse response is always symmetric, h[k] = h[N-1-k].

options: Systolic symmetric form: A/ACOUT input cascade + PCOUT partial-sum cascade, pre-adder per DSP
Transposed form: input broadcast to all DSPs, partial sums in PCOUT chain
decisions.choice: Systolic symmetric form using the DSP48E2 pre-adder, ACOUT/ACIN delay-line cascade and PCOUT/PCIN adder chain
decisions.rationale: Transposed form needs the input broadcast to every DSP (high fanout at 491.52 MHz across up to 32 DSPs) and does not combine cleanly with the pre-adder for symmetry. Systolic keeps routing on dedicated cascades and uses ceil(N/2) DSPs with no fabric adder tree, at ~N/2 extra cycles of latency the spec tolerates.
decisions.question: Do you accept the systolic symmetric form (pre-adder + A and P cascades, ~N/2 extra cycles latency) over the transposed form?

options: Centre tap in a DSP with pre-adder second operand forced to zero
Centre tap with pre-adder bypassed
Centre tap multiplier in fabric
decisions.choice: Centre tap occupies the last DSP of the chain with the D (second pre-adder) operand held at zero, keeping a uniform cascade
decisions.rationale: Keeps every stage identical and the cascade unbroken; costs no extra DSP versus ceil(N/2).
decisions.question: For odd N, is it acceptable that the centre tap uses a full DSP slice with one pre-adder input tied to zero?

done_when: A comparison table (DSP count, fabric adders, input fanout, cascade usage, latency, Fmax risk) for transposed vs systolic is written with the final call
Block diagram shows ceil(N_TAPS/2) DSP48E2 stages, ACOUT and PCOUT cascades, the source of the mirrored sample for each pre-adder (e.g. fabric SRL delay line), and the output stage
Even and odd N_TAPS chains are both drawn or described, including the centre-tap stage and the N_TAPS=2/3 degenerate chains
Fabric resources outside DSPs (delay lines, registers) are estimated for N_TAPS=16 and N_TAPS=64

steps.title: Bit-growth analysis from Q1.15 x Q1.17 through the 48-bit P cascade
steps.goal: Derive the width at every datapath point (pre-adder, multiplier, cascade accumulator, output) and justify that nothing overflows inside the DSP chain for N_TAPS up to 64.

spec_evidence.quote: Provide a bit-growth analysis and justify the internal widths.
Coefficients: 18-bit signed, Q1.17.
Input: 16-bit signed samples, Q1.15. Output: 16-bit signed, Q1.15.

options: Full precision through pre-adder, multiplier and P cascade; single quantisation at the output
Truncate/round partial sums inside the chain
decisions.choice: Full precision: 17-bit pre-add (Q2.15), 35-bit product (Q3.32), accumulation in the 48-bit P cascade (about 40 bits needed for 32 products), quantised once at the output
decisions.rationale: All widths fit DSP48E2 natively (27-bit pre-adder, 27x18 multiplier, 48-bit P), so full precision is free and the output is exactly one rounding of the ideal result.
decisions.question: Is a single rounding at the output (full precision inside the DSP chain) acceptable, or is there a required internal noise/precision budget?

done_when: A width table lists format (Qm.n) and bit count at pre-adder out, multiplier out and accumulator for general N_TAPS, with worst-case values for N_TAPS=16 and N_TAPS=64
Worst-case accumulator magnitude is bounded both by generic ceil(log2(N_TAPS/2)) growth and by sum|h[k]|, and shown to fit 48 bits
Bit position of the Q1.15 output inside the accumulator (LSBs dropped, guard bits above) is identified

steps.title: Round-to-nearest and saturating output stage
steps.goal: Specify how the accumulator is rounded to 16 bits and saturated (not wrapped), and where those operations live (DSP vs fabric), without breaking 491.52 MHz timing.

spec_evidence.quote: Outputs must saturate, not wrap.
Rounding to nearest.

options: Round-half-up: add 0.5 LSB constant injected at the head of the P cascade
Convergent (round-half-even) using DSP pattern detect
Rounding adder in fabric after the chain
decisions.choice: Round-half-up by injecting a constant 2^(k-1) into the first DSP of the chain (C port or RND), then truncate; saturation by guard-bit compare (fabric or DSP pattern detect) in a registered output stage
decisions.rationale: Bias injection costs zero extra adders or cycles; half-up tie bias is negligible with 17 dropped bits. Saturation detection is a small registered stage that keeps timing.
decisions.question: Is round-half-up acceptable for 'rounding to nearest', or do you require convergent (round-half-even) rounding?

done_when: Rounding constant value and injection point are specified
Saturation condition (guard bits not all equal to sign) and clamp values 0x7FFF/0x8000 are specified
Number of pipeline registers in the output stage is stated and fed into the latency count

steps.title: Glitch-free shadow-bank commit aligned to the systolic skew
steps.goal: Design the per-instance coefficient write path so every output sample uses only old or only new coefficients, accounting for each output's partial products being formed in different DSPs on different cycles.

spec_evidence.quote: Changing the filter must not create a glitch: no output sample may be computed from a mix of old and new coefficients.
They must be loadable at run time from the control processor (via a simple write port; the AXI-Lite wrapper exists already).

options: Shadow bank + commit token that propagates down the DSP chain with the same skew as the partial sum
Shadow bank swapped in all DSPs on the same cycle
Flush/blank the output during reload
decisions.choice: Shadow coefficient registers per tap; on commit, a swap token travels along the chain one stage per partial-sum delay, loading each DSP's active B register exactly when the first post-commit output's partial sum reaches it
decisions.rationale: The user answer confirms a shadow bank plus commit; a simultaneous swap in a systolic chain would mix coefficients for in-flight outputs, so a skewed token places the boundary between two output samples with no blanking.
decisions.question: Is a coefficient change that takes effect seamlessly on a sample boundary (no output blanking) required, or would muting/flushing the output during reload be acceptable?

options: Explicit commit write (strobe/register) after loading all coefficients
Implicit commit on write to the last coefficient address
decisions.choice: Explicit commit strobe on the write port; writes before commit only touch the shadow bank
decisions.rationale: Consistent with the user's 'shadow bank and commit' wording; allows partial or out-of-order reloads and atomic broadcast commits across all 32 channels from the wrapper.
decisions.question: Should new coefficients take effect on an explicit 'commit' write, or automatically when the last coefficient is written?

decisions.topic: Clock domain of the coefficient write port
options: Write port synchronous to the 491.52 MHz fabric clock (wrapper does CDC)
Write port in the AXI-Lite clock domain with CDC inside FIR-01
decisions.choice: Write port is synchronous to the fabric clock; the existing AXI-Lite wrapper performs any clock crossing
decisions.rationale: Keeps FIR-01 single-clock; with broadcast, one crossing in the wrapper serves all 32 instances.
decisions.question: Does the existing AXI-Lite wrapper present the coefficient write port in the 491.52 MHz fabric clock domain, or must FIR-01 accept writes in the AXI clock domain?

done_when: Timing diagram shows commit, token propagation and the first output sample fully using new coefficients
Argument that token delay per stage equals partial-sum delay per stage for both even and odd N_TAPS
Behaviour for writes arriving while a swap is in flight, and for commit with no prior writes, is specified
Use of DSP48E2 B1/B2 registers or fabric shadow registers is chosen and resource cost stated
A broadcast commit is shown to switch all 32 channels on the same input sample index

steps.title: Behaviour when the decimator valid drops
steps.goal: Define how in_valid gaps affect filter state and out_valid so the filter output equals the FIR of the valid-only sample stream.

spec_evidence.quote: The upstream decimator provides a valid signal.
In this product it is always high once running, but the filter must behave sensibly if it drops.

options: Global clock-enable: whole pipeline (DSP CE pins, delay lines, swap token, output stage) advances only when in_valid=1; out_valid is the delayed valid
Free-running pipeline treating invalid cycles as zero samples
Free-running pipeline with out_valid only (state corrupted by gaps)
decisions.choice: Global clock-enable driven by registered in_valid with replicated CE registers to meet fanout at 491.52 MHz; out_valid tracks the enabled pipeline so outputs equal the FIR of valid samples only
decisions.rationale: Keeps the systolic alignment intact across gaps and gives mathematically correct output; DSP48E2 has per-register CE pins so cost is mostly CE fanout.
decisions.question: When input valid drops, should the filter stall (state frozen, output = FIR of only the valid samples), or is treating missing samples as zeros acceptable?

done_when: Every stateful element is classified as CE-gated or free-running, including the coefficient swap token
out_valid generation and its relation to in_valid are specified with a timing diagram showing a gap
CE fanout/replication plan for ceil(N_TAPS/2) DSPs at 491.52 MHz is stated
Latency is stated in valid samples (constant) as well as clock cycles when valid=1

steps.title: Pipeline register map and constant-latency budget under 100 ns
steps.goal: Enumerate every register from input to output and prove a constant latency below 49 cycles (100 ns at 491.52 MHz) for N_TAPS up to 64.

spec_evidence.quote: Latency is not critical (< 100 ns is fine) but must be constant and documented.
one new sample every clock, 491.52 MHz on a Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoC

done_when: Register-by-register list (input reg, A1/A2, AD, M, P per stage, output stage) is given
Latency formula L(N_TAPS) in cycles is given and evaluated for N_TAPS=2, 16 and 64, with ns values, all <100 ns
Statement that latency is fixed per build and independent of coefficient values, commit timing and valid pattern (in valid samples)
DSP48E2 internal registers used to meet 491.52 MHz are identified (fully pipelined mode)

steps.title: Single fabric clock and minimal-reset strategy for DSP-heavy datapath
steps.goal: Define the clock and reset scheme: one 491.52 MHz clock, which registers are reset, and what outputs and coefficient banks look like during and after reset.

spec_evidence.quote: one new sample every clock, 491.52 MHz on a Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoC
In this product it is always high once running, but the filter must behave sensibly if it drops.

options: Synchronous reset on control only (valid pipeline, swap token, commit state); datapath and DSP registers unreset, outputs masked by out_valid
Synchronous reset of all registers including DSP pipeline and coefficient banks
decisions.choice: Synchronous active-high reset on control state only; datapath/DSP registers not reset; out_valid held low until the pipeline has filled with valid samples; coefficient banks retain or reset to a documented default
decisions.rationale: Xilinx guidance for high-Fmax DSP datapaths; avoids reset fanout to ceil(N/2) DSPs in each of 32 instances while outputs remain well-defined via out_valid.
decisions.question: Is it acceptable that after reset the datapath is not cleared and out_valid stays low until N valid samples have filled the filter, or must the output be exactly zero-state filtered from reset?

done_when: Clock domain(s) listed with frequency; any CDC delegated to the wrapper is stated
Reset polarity, synchronicity and the list of reset vs non-reset registers are given
Post-reset contents of active and shadow coefficient banks and out_valid behaviour until pipeline fill are specified

steps.title: Corner cases: overflow coefficients, swap during gaps, N_TAPS extremes
steps.goal: Enumerate and resolve edge conditions so the MA defines behaviour everywhere.

spec_evidence.quote: Outputs must saturate, not wrap.
Both even and odd N must be supported.
Changing the filter must not create a glitch: no output sample may be computed from a mix of old and new coefficients.

done_when: Cases covered: full-scale inputs with sum|h|>1 (saturation), -1.0 inputs pre-added (-2.0 fits 17 bits), N_TAPS=2/3/63/64, commit while valid is low, back-to-back commits, broadcast commit while one channel's valid differs, writes to out-of-range addresses
Each case has a defined outcome and the mechanism that guarantees it

no output sample may be computed from a mix of old and new coefficients.
